newsitem.title: USA: CBOT to place Project A terminals in London.
newsitem.headline: CBOT to place Project A terminals in London.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade has received approval from British regulators to place Project A electronic trading terminals in London, CBOT Chairman Patrick Arbor said Thursday.
"Project A has proven to be a dynamic, successful tool for expanding the Board of Trade's reach during our off-market hours," Arbor told exchange members at a midyear chairman's address.

The fast-growing Project A system, which matches bids and offers electronically, has reached average volume of 20,000 contracts a day this year, despite a modest distribution of 187 workstations, Arbor noted.
New trading firms continue to join the system and now total 67, of which 22 are primary dealers, he added.
Arbor said an exchange committee next month would craft a policy to determine how profits from the Ceres Trading Limited Partnership that governs the Project A system will be distributed.
The CBOT chairman said he would recommend distributions be made annually, following an initial payout of $1,000 per full member.
